A_target.statement:
Let $f: A \to B$ and $g: B \to A$ be [[Definition:Injection|injections]].
Then there exists a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] $h: A \to B$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {L, \preceq}$ be a [[Definition:Complete Lattice|complete lattice]] and $F: L \to L$ [[Definition:Increasing Mapping|increasing]].
Then $F$ has a [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed point]].

substitutions.complete lattice: the power set P(A) ordered by inclusion
substitutions.monotone map F: F(S) = A minus g(B minus f(S))

derived.fixed point S = F(S): a set on which to splice f and g into a bijection
derived.the fixed set: region where the bijection uses f, complement uses g^{-1}

object_map.reformulation: Encode the desired splitting of A as a fixed point of the monotone operator F(S) = A - g(B - f(S)) on the power-set lattice.

validity_conditions: P(A) under inclusion is a complete lattice; F(S) = A - g(B - f(S)) is monotone (two complements compose to preserve order).
Knaster-Tarski gives a fixed set S* with S* = A - g(B - f(S*)).
On S* use f, on its complement use g^{-1}; injectivity of f,g makes the spliced map a bijection.
proof_plan: Work in the complete lattice $\struct {\powerset A, \subseteq}$.

Define:
:$\map F S = A \setminus \map g {B \setminus \map f S}$
If $S \subseteq T$ then $\map f S \subseteq \map f T$, so $B \setminus \map f T \subseteq B \setminus \map f S$, and $\map F S \subseteq \map F T$.
Hence $F$ is [[Definition:Increasing Mapping|increasing]].

By the [[Knaster-Tarski Theorem]], there exists $S^*$ with $\map F {S^*} = S^*$.
Then $A \setminus S^* = \map g {B \setminus \map f {S^*} }$.

Define:
:$\map h x = \begin {cases} \map f x & : x \in S^* \\ \map {g^{-1} } x & : x \in A \setminus S^* \end {cases}$
$h$ maps $S^*$ bijectively onto $\map f {S^*}$ and $A \setminus S^*$ bijectively onto $B \setminus \map f {S^*}$.
Hence $h$ is a bijection, which is the [[Cantor-Bernstein-Schröder Theorem]].
{{qed}}
